title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: proof 1 — through one man ≠ Adam's actual named
pass_a_gloss: Four strokes, so far as I can count them. First: 'one man' means Adam the first; therefore the sin that entered through one man is Adam's first actual. The consequence fails. Paul never writes 'Adam's sin' here; he writes that through Adam sin entered the World. Adam is cast as cause, the World (humans) as subject. He is not ranking who first sinned on earth—Eve before Adam, the devil before Eve—but teaching that through Adam sin's corruption was brought in upon all.
pass_b_english: You use, as far as I can gather, four arguments. 1. By one man the Apostle understands the first man, namely Adam. Therefore by the sin which entered into the World through one man he understands Adam's first actual sin. I deny that it follows. For the Apostle does not say Adam's sin, but that through Adam sin entered into the World. He considers Adam as the cause of this sin, the World—that is, humans—as the subject: nor did he wish to teach who first sinned in the World (for Eve before Adam, and before her the devil, sinned) but that through Adam the corruption of sin was introduced into all humans.
source_text: Uteris, quantum colligere possum, quatuor argumentis. 1. Per unum hominem Apostolus intelligit primum hominem scilicet Adamum. Ergo per peccatum quod per unum hominem introiit in Mundum intelligit primum peccatum actuale Adami. Nego sequi. Non enim Apostolus dicit Adami peccatum, sed per Adamum peccatum introiisse in Mundum. Adamum considerat ut huius peccati causam, Mundum, id est, homines ut subiectum: nec docere voluit, quis primus in Mundo peccaverit (nam Adamo prior Eva, & hac prior diabolus peccavit) sed in omnes homines per Adamum introductam esse corruptionem peccati.

choices.choice: Through one man as cause ≠ naming Adam's actual
